title: He didn’t answer you… and you called that silence.
paragraphs: He didn’t answer you… and you called that silence.
But what if it was love?
What if the quiet you hate… is the mercy you don’t yet understand?

No voice.
No breakthrough.
No miracle.
And slowly, a dangerous thought crept in:

Because some of the most loving things God does…
feel like nothing at all.
You didn’t fall into that sin again.
No voice from heaven said, “Well done.”
Just a quiet strength you didn’t have before.
You thought God was ignoring you.
But what if He was protecting you from something you couldn’t see?
From a relationship that would have broken you.
From a decision that would have cost you your calling.
From a path that looked good… but led to quiet destruction.
We don’t struggle with God’s absence.
But God often moves in whispers.
“The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases; His mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning.” — Lamentations 3:22–23
Not just when you feel Him.
Not just when you see results.
Not just when life makes sense.
Every morning, mercy is already waiting for you.
Even when you don’t recognize it.
And here’s the part we don’t like:
Sometimes God’s greatest love is what He didn’t allow.
The sin you were about to commit.
The breakdown you were close to having.
The opportunity that looked perfect… but wasn’t from Him.
But He’s been intervening all along.
But let’s not stay at the surface.

Because the loudest proof of God’s love…
was not a whisper.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Not when you finally “got your life together.”
While you were still in sin.
You and I were not just struggling—we were separated.
It’s rebellion against a holy God.
And no amount of self-improvement could fix that.
Lived the life you couldn’t live.
Absorbed the wrath meant for you.
God’s love is not proven by how loud your season is.

And if the cross is real—
then your silence is not abandonment.
It might be God working in ways your eyes cannot yet see.
Some scholars interpret God’s “still small voice” in 1 Kings 19:12 as a reminder that His presence is often gentle, not overwhelming—personal, not performative.
Not everything God does is meant to impress you.
Some things are meant to transform you.
So before you say, “God is not speaking…”
Have I been too loud to hear Him?

Too focused on what He hasn’t done…
that I missed what He already did?
Still being drawn back to Him.
And maybe today, God is doing something deeper than giving you answers.
Lay down the sin you’ve been hiding.
The control you refuse to release.
Because the same Jesus who died for you…
And His voice is still reaching you.
He was loving you all along.
